title: E2 answerability gate -- pre-registered calibration and holdout verdict
lane: Market-No.1 program W2-E2, workstream E, item E2 (PROGRAM-2026-11-04.md §4.E)
claim: None until the holdout receipt exists. The verdict is SUPPORTED or NOT_SUPPORTED by the rule below and is published either way. Nothing is tuned after the holdout is read; a later change is a new revision and a new holdout, never a substitution.
question: Does the deterministic answerability gate, shadowed on the Ask route, refuse questions the World cannot answer often enough to lower the wrong-answer rate on unanswerable questions, without refusing more than a pre-registered share of answerable ones?

split.rule: E1's own frozen split: every question's `split` field, set by gen_xbrl_questions.mjs splitOf(id) = parity of the first 32 bits of sha256(id). No PRNG and no seed of E2's own: the split is a pure function of the question id, recorded before E2 existed, and E2 does not re-split.
split.seed: none (deterministic sha256(id) parity, E1 PREREG revision 2 `split`)
split.holdoutIdsDigestRule: sha256 of the holdout question ids, sorted, joined by \n
split.use: The coverage threshold is chosen on calibration only. The calibration phase never replays a holdout question. The holdout is replayed once, after the calibration receipt is committed, with that receipt's threshold.

corpus.description: One collection per corpusRef: the filer's two pinned 10-K primary documents (E1 questions/xbrl-numeric.json#filers), read from eval/ask-quality/cache (git-ignored) and verified by sha256 before use.
corpus.chunking: eval/ask-quality/e2/e2.ts chunkDocument: visible text only (ix:header, script, style, comments removed); consecutive text blocks packed into chunks of at most 400 characters on word boundaries; each table packed apart from text, row by row, every chunk prefixed with the table's header (the first of its first five rows that names a year 1900-2199 and is at most 150 characters). 400 keeps three citations inside the fallback's 3 x 420 answer envelope, so a baseline abstention is a retrieval outcome, not an envelope overflow.
corpus.notProduction: Production compiles OCR regions of a PDF; this is an HTML chunking of the same filings. pageNumber1 = 1 and bbox1000 = [0,0,1000,1000] on every chunk are placeholders the chunk schema requires and nothing reads.

retriever.function: lib/grounded-ask.ts answerGroundedQuestion -- the Ask route's excerpt-concatenation-fallback path, run in process on the built artifact (no network, no database, no model)
retriever.goldHit: answerable only: some citation's 420-character excerpt contains a gold span by E1 score.ts containsSpan (numeric spans as whole numbers)
retriever.notCovered: The compiled-retrieval-v1 path (RRF, reranker, World Gate, held conflicts) is not replayed; the verdict speaks for the fallback path only.

gate.input: question; evidence = the cited chunks' full text in citation order; heldConflicts = null (the fallback reads none); worldCoverage = {processedSources: 2, unprocessedSources: 0}
rules: 3. the question asks for an amount (quantity words or a currency/percent unit) and no single evidence item states an amount (digits left after removing month-name dates, ISO/slash dates, Item/Note/Part/Schedule/Exhibit/Page references and years) together with every year 1900-2199 the question names -> NOT_IN_WORLD (NO_NUMERIC_ANCHOR)
4. termCoverage = |question tokens found in the evidence tokens| / |question tokens| (lib/lexical-tokens.ts tokens, unique) below the threshold -> PARTIAL (TERM_COVERAGE_BELOW_THRESHOLD)
5. otherwise ANSWERABLE. OUT_OF_SCHEMA is never produced (no certified schema exists).
gate.refuse: PRIMARY: status in {NOT_IN_WORLD, PARTIAL, OUT_OF_SCHEMA} (lib/answerability.ts REFUSING_STATUSES). SECONDARY, reported and never gating: {NOT_IN_WORLD, OUT_OF_SCHEMA}, the narrower set PROGRAM §4.E names for its canary.
gate.notAScalar: No blind quality score: the verdict is a fixed rule order over named features, and termCoverage is one feature with its covered and missing terms reported.

calibration.grid: 0, then 0.500 to 1.000 in steps of 0.025 (22 values; e2.ts THRESHOLD_GRID)
calibration.rule: On the calibration split: among thresholds whose refused-answerable share (answerable refused / answerable) is <= 0.05, choose the one that refuses the most unanswerable questions; ties go to the smaller threshold. If none is feasible, the threshold is 0 (coverage rule off) and the receipt records constraintMet = false; the holdout still runs and the criteria decide.
calibration.output: eval/ask-quality/e2/receipts/calibration-<run time>-<receipt sha>.json, committed before the holdout phase runs

holdoutMetrics.numerator: unanswerable the baseline answered and the gate did not refuse
answerable with a baseline gold-span hit that the gate refused
holdoutMetrics.denominator: answerable holdout questions with a baseline gold-span hit

holdoutMetrics.numerator: answerable with a baseline gold-span hit
refused unanswerable of that generation rule
holdoutMetrics.denominator: unanswerable holdout questions of that rule

statistics.zeroDenominator: value null, interval null, criterion NOT_EVALUABLE
statistics.note: E1's numeric exact match is not used: evidence_excerpts returns passages, not values, so correct_over_answerable is ~0 by construction (E1 PREREG); the gold-span hit stands in for 'a correct answer was served', and E1 statistics.e2Gate asks for exactly these rates to be read together.

passCriteria.C1: Wilson95 upper(gated_wrong_answer_over_unanswerable) < Wilson95 lower(baseline_wrong_answer_over_unanswerable) -- the wrong-answer rate falls with non-overlapping intervals (PROGRAM §4.E 'lower than baseline (CI)')
passCriteria.C2: Wilson95 upper(refused_over_answerable) <= 0.10 -- the pre-registered tolerance for answerable questions lost (PROGRAM §4.E 'loss <= pre-registered tolerance')
passCriteria.C3: Wilson95 upper(gold_span_hits_lost) <= 0.10 -- the same tolerance on the answerable questions the baseline actually served the gold evidence for
passCriteria.verdict: SUPPORTED iff C1, C2 and C3 all PASS. Any FAIL or NOT_EVALUABLE -> NOT_SUPPORTED, published as NOT_SUPPORTED in the lane report with every rate and its denominator.

pinnedCodeRule: sha256 of each file's text with CRLF read as LF, so a Windows checkout and CI agree. run_e2.mjs refuses to run when any differs.
limitations: One retriever (the fallback), one chunking of HTML, four filers, XBRL-template questions: a verdict here says nothing about the compiled path, PDFs, other corpora or human questions.
Rules 2 and the OUT_OF_SCHEMA status are not exercised: no conflicts, no certified schema.
Questions cluster by filing; Wilson intervals treat them as independent and understate the uncertainty.
The threshold is set on one corpus; it is not 'calibrated' in the CalibrationTable sense and is never presented as such.
production: The Ask route shadows the gate behind TAVONEL_ASK_ANSWERABILITY_MODE (off | shadow; default off) and never changes the served answer. `on` is not built; it may only be proposed after a SUPPORTED verdict and a reviewed change.
